# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

   park it wears *is* the in-review state and the failure park *is* the report (which
   is why `--pr` is still required on an approval — a park nobody can act on is not
   a park). The standing status is also what stops the next scheduler run adopting
   the same issue again; clearing it is a person's decision, made after reading what
   the run said. Only an item filed under the older shadow model writes back to a
   different issue, and the command does that too.

   Only `task:status:needs-human-failure` (and a park whose kind cannot be decoded) holds the
   task's lane — while one is open the generator files no further occurrence of
   this task. The other three wait for their human while the schedule carries on,
   so leaving one open costs nobody but the person it names.

   The `claudinite-task-exec` record goes onto the item, in the same comment, and
   the command writes it — Actions logs expire and the item does not, so the item
   is where a record has to live. Nothing here is yours to print by hand.

7. **Capture this session before you end it.** Last step, after the item is
   converged, and run it whichever way step 6 went:

   ```bash
   CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE=<n> node <engine>/hooks/session-end-command.mjs
   ```

   That runner invokes whatever session-end steps this repo's declared packs
   contribute; it knows nothing about what any of them do, and a repo that
   contributes none does nothing. Nobody is sitting in front of this session, so it
   ends by having its container reclaimed — precisely the ending that fires no
   `SessionEnd` hook. Left to the hook, every unattended run would leave no record
   of itself anywhere: not of the skills it loaded, not of the checks that caught
   something, not of how the work actually went, and not of the record you just
   printed. `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE` is what files those logs under the item that
   ran, rather than under nothing.

   It cannot fail your run — the item is already converged and this changes nothing
   on GitHub. If it reports an error, **say so plainly in your final message** and
   end anyway.

## The one standing bound

You execute **this one item and nothing else**. Never list other work items,
never sweep the queue, never act on a second issue in this session — however
obviously stuck another one looks. Recovery is code that runs elsewhere, and a
session that helps out is how one item becomes three duplicate PRs.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.

Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).

Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).

Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.

Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. #1262 rewrote the worker docs of `growth-extract`, `growth-discover-packs`, `prose-to-checks-sweep`, `rule-revalidation` and `growth-dedup` so that a change to a local pack is recorded as a row in that pack's own `VERSIONS.md`, in the same commit, rather than as a dated comment on a standing `Claudinite tracker: ` issue.

```
Original-issue: #1258
In-production-when: a PR titled `Claudinite growth: extract lessons …` (or any `Claudinite growth:` capture run) has MERGED in missingbulb/Claudinite with a merge time later than 2026-08-23T01:10:00Z. Read the merged PR's own file list; a scheduler run that declined, or a run that found nothing to add, is not this condition — keep waiting for one that actually changed a local pack.
Verify: that merged PR's diff touches `.claudinite/local/packs//VERSIONS.md`, adding at least one row naming the task and what landed. Pass = such a row is present AND no comment was posted to any `Claudinite tracker:` issue by that run. Fail = the run changed a local pack's RULES.md or declared-checks.json but added no VERSIONS.md row, or it posted to a tracker issue instead.
Not-before: 2026-08-25T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day
```

Note for the run: a `Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract` issue may still exist from before this change. Its continued existence is not a failure — nothing deletes it. What fails is a **new** comment on it dated after the merge above.

## How to converge

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the repo's merged PRs. Never infer it from a merge of #1262 itself, a green run, or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence you actually read (the PR number, the VERSIONS.md rows it added) and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen #1258 with a comment saying what was asserted, what the run did instead and which PR you read; comment here linking that; close this issue as completed.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

`growth-extract` run over this window's Context: commits f922772/9fedbed/3f76817, merged PRs #1398/#1397/#1422, touched PR #1419, touched issues #1346/#1237/#1236/#1119/#1400/#1420, plus the conversation-logs fresh window (issue-1417, 1421, 1392, 1395, 1431, 1425) and the oldest-24h hindsight window (issue-349, 359, 366, 364, 368, 373).

**Activity half — two additions to `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`** (the engine/mount section and the proving-a-change section):

- **Adding a key to the declared-check spec vocabulary** — bump every emitting pack's `minEngineVersion` to the release that adds it, or an older engine's unknown-key throw drops every declaration in the file and wedges the member's convergence until a human deletes it by hand. From #1400 (still open — a design decision on the real fix hasn't landed yet, so this is the interim caution).
- **Sweeping a rename mid-migration across many PRs** — a file added or rewritten after the sweep starts can independently reinvent the retired constant as a comparison key; the comparison then fails silently, no error, only a wrong count. From #1119's re-land (PR #1385 caught `claudinite-dashboard/work.mjs` and `next-work.mjs` doing exactly this with the retired `NEEDS_HUMAN` label constant).

Neither converts to a check: (A)'s signature doesn't exist yet (no per-key "added-since" data, and the underlying fix in #1400 is undecided); (B) is a caution about future, arbitrary rewrites rather than a fixed pattern with a stable signature.

**Conversation half — nothing new.** The fresh window's unattended-task logs (1417, 1421, 1431, 1425) ran clean; the two owner-driven sessions (1392, 1395) surfaced only friction already covered by standing rules (stacked-PR version-bump collision, `add_repo` scope widening). The oldest-24h hindsight window (all from 2026-07-19/20) is the origin conversation behind several rules already in the pack (`barriers`/pack-independence, "an owner reversing a standing decision", `Edit` requiring a prior `Read`, the no-padded-`sleep` guard) — nothing there is uncaptured. No comment posted on any conversation-log issue, since nothing landed from that half.

**Upgrade pass** — ran `prose-to-checks`'s two gates against both new bullets; neither clears the check-the-world test (see above), so both stay prose.

Verified: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2678/2679 (the one failure is `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs`'s pre-existing shallow-clone guard, unrelated to this diff). `check_the_work` clean. `check_the_world` — 0 blocking, 83 advisory, none naming these files beyond one pre-existing line-length advisory at an unrelated line in the same file.

   records, and re-render generated files rather than editing them by hand.

+  starts can independently reinvent the retired constant as a comparison key; a state comparison

{"number":1258,"title":"Retire the standing tracker issue from the growth, wiki and jwt tasks — the local pack's own VERSIONS.md is the record","body":"Eleven tasks keep a standing tracker issue. Most of them are logging what automatic work did to a **local pack** — which belongs in the pack, in git, not in an issue body nobody opens.

## What changes

| Task | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-extract` | `Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract` | no issue; a `VERSIONS.md` line per rule added |
| `growth-discover-packs` | `Claudinite tracker: Discover Local Packs` | no issue; seeds the new pack's `VERSIONS.md` |
| `prose-to-checks-sweep` | `Claudinite tracker: Prose to Checks` | no issue; a `VERSIONS.md` line per check created |
| `rule-revalidation` | `Claudinite tracker: Rule Revalidation` | no issue, **no slicing** — probe every claim each run; a `VERSIONS.md` line per rule corrected or deleted |
| `growth-dedup` | `Claudinite tracker: Growth Dedup` | no standing issue; the window brief becomes a comment on the run's own work item; a `VERSIONS.md` line per rule removed |
| `wiki-growth` | `Claudinite tracker: Product Wiki Growth` | no issue — the wiki's git history is the record |
| `jwt-advisory-watch` | `Claudinite tracker: JWT advisory watch` | no standing issue; files a **real** issue only when an advisory hits a pinned version |
| `tidy-issues`, `tidy-prs` | keep | keep |
| `tidy-branches` | keep | untouched — #1240 removes the task |
| `ci-performance` | `[claudinite] CI performance` | keep — it is a live measurement table, not a growth log |

## The record that replaces them

`VERSIONS.md` at the root of each local pack (`.claudinite/local/packs//VERSIONS.md`): every addition or removal of a prose rule, and every check created, by whichever automatic task did it. One dated line per change, newest first. It is in the pack, so it travels with the pack, diffs in a PR, and survives an issue sweep.

## Two engine fixes that come with it

- `findTracker`/`findOrCreateTracker` re-close any tracker they find **open**. `createTracker` has closed on create since #951, but nothing ever repaired a tracker created before that — which is why #904 has sat open since 2026-08-16.
- `[claudinite] CI performance` is added to the hidden-titles filter in `engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`. It is off-convention, so `tidy-issues` currently sees it as ordinary project work.

## Why `growth-dedup` cannot simply drop its issue

Its tracker is not a log — it is the carrier for the window brief, because there is no code→agent data channel (`worker.mjs:16`). Code-work already receives `CLAUDINITE_ITEM`, the work item's own issue number, so the brief becomes a comment there: per-run, which is what the brief already is, and it dies with the item.

## Why `rule-revalidation` loses its slicing

`task.md:34` picks the ten claims longest since their last recorded probe **per the tracker's log**. The tracker is state, not a record. A weekly run that probes every environment-fact claim needs no memory, and the judgment prose is already out of scope — so the set is far smaller than the corpus.","state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1258","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-23T00:44:36Z","updated_at":"2026-08-23T01:08:08Z","closed_at":"2026-08-23T01:08:08Z","closed_by":"missingbulb","has_parent":false,"has_children":true,"sub_issues_summary":{"total":2,"completed":0,"percent_completed":0},"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":1,"references":[{"number":1262,"title":"Retire the growth, wiki and jwt standing trackers for the pack's VERSIONS.md","state":"MERGED","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1262","repository":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}]}}

Most of them are logging what automatic work did to a **local pack** — which belongs in the pack, in git, not in an issue body nobody opens.

## What changes

| Task | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-extract` | `Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract` | no issue; a `VERSIONS.md` line per rule added |
| `growth-discover-packs` | `Claudinite tracker: Discover Local Packs` | no issue; seeds the new pack's `VERSIONS.md` |
| `prose-to-checks-sweep` | `Claudinite tracker: Prose to Checks` | no issue; a `VERSIONS.md` line per check created |
| `rule-revalidation` | `Claudinite tracker: Rule Revalidation` | no issue, **no slicing** — probe every claim each run; a `VERSIONS.md` line per rule corrected or deleted |
| `growth-dedup` | `Claudinite tracker: Growth Dedup` | no standing issue; the window brief becomes a comment on the run's own work item; a `VERSIONS.md` line per rule removed |
| `wiki-growth` | `Claudinite tracker: Product Wiki Growth` | no issue — the wiki's git history is the record |
| `jwt-advisory-watch` | `Claudinite tracker: JWT advisory watch` | no standing issue; files a **real** issue only when an advisory hits a pinned version |
| `tidy-issues`, `tidy-prs` | keep | keep |
| `tidy-branches` | keep | untouched — #1240 removes the task |
| `ci-performance` | `[claudinite] CI performance` | keep — it is a live measurement table, not a growth log |

## The record that replaces them

`VERSIONS.md` at the root of each local pack (`.claudinite/local/packs//VERSIONS.md`): every addition or removal of a prose rule, and every check created, by whichever automatic task did it. One dated line per change, newest first. It is in the pack, so it travels with the pack, diffs in a PR, and survives an issue sweep.

## Two engine fixes that come with it

- `findTracker`/`findOrCreateTracker` re-close any tracker they find **open**. `createTracker` has closed on create since #951, but nothing ever repaired a tracker created before that — which is why #904 has sat open since 2026-08-16.
- `[claudinite] CI performance` is added to the hidden-titles filter in `engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`. It is off-convention, so `tidy-issues` currently sees it as ordinary project work.

## Why `growth-dedup` cannot simply drop its issue

Its tracker is not a log — it is the carrier for the window brief, because there is no code→agent data channel (`worker.mjs:16`). Code-work already receives `CLAUDINITE_ITEM`, the work item's own issue number, so the brief becomes a comment there: per-run, which is what the brief already is, and it dies with the item.

## Why `rule-revalidation` loses its slicing

`task.md:34` picks the ten claims longest since their last recorded probe **per the tracker's log**. The tracker is state, not a record. A weekly run that probes every environment-fact claim needs no memory, and the judgment prose is already out of scope — so the set is far smaller than the corpus.","state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1258","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-23T00:44:36Z","updated_at":"2026-08-23T01:08:08Z","closed_at":"2026-08-23T01:08:08Z","closed_by":"missingbulb","has_parent":false,"has_children":true,"sub_issues_summary":{"total":2,"completed":0,"percent_completed":0},"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":1,"references":[{"number":1262,"title":"Retire the growth, wiki and jwt standing trackers for the pack's VERSIONS.md","state":"MERGED","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1262","repository":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}]}}
